title: Learning to Fail
topic: ประสบการณ์ส่วนตัว
lines: In my last year of high school, I applied for a scholarship to study
engineering. I had good grades, and my teachers were sure I would get
**it**. I did not. When the results came out, my name was not on the list.
For two weeks I hardly left my room. I felt I had let everyone down,
especially my parents, who had worked extra hours to pay for my tutoring.
It was my grandmother who finally pulled me out. She did not tell me to
cheer up. Instead, she asked me to help **her** in her vegetable garden
every morning. While we worked, she told me about her own failures: the
shop she had opened and lost, and the years she had spent rebuilding.
"**Those** were not wasted years," she said. "They taught me what I could
survive." Slowly, I started to study again. The next year I applied to
three universities and was accepted by **two**. Now, when I fail a test, I
still feel bad, but I no longer think **it** says anything final about me.
It is just information about what I need to do next.
